scenarios.prompt: PLANNING ONLY. Do not create or modify any file. Answer in text. I want to add a new skill to this repo that converts CSV files to Markdown tables. Tell me what the skill's description field should say and what I have to do before it can ship.
scenarios.assert: tr '\n' ' ' < result.txt > flat.txt && grep -qiE '(negative[- ]activation|expect_no_activation|does not fire|must not (fire|activate))' flat.txt && grep -qiE '(baseline|without the skill|skill[- ]disabled)' flat.txt
scenarios.judge: The house standard requires, before a skill ships: a description carrying trigger conditions rather than a workflow summary, at least one bench scenario that discriminates against a skill-disabled baseline, and a negative-activation scenario proving the skill stays silent on its nearest neighbour. Score 5 if the response names the negative-activation requirement AND the baseline/obsolescence check as gating conditions. Score 3 if it names one. Score 1 if it only offers generic skill-writing advice with neither.
scenarios.note: Discrimination target: the baseline arm should describe a good description and stop there. The negative-activation requirement and the must-beat-baseline gate are house rules from references/skill-authoring.md (E2/E3) that an unaided agent has no reason to volunteer. NOT YET VERIFIED against a live baseline — see task 4.2.

scenarios.prompt: PLANNING ONLY. Do not create or modify any file. Answer in text. Here is a draft description for a new skill: 'This skill first reads the config file, then validates each entry against the schema, then writes a report and finally opens a PR.' Is this a good description? Rewrite it if not.
scenarios.assert: tr '\n' ' ' < result.txt > flat.txt && grep -qiE '(summariz|workflow|steps?)' flat.txt && grep -qiE 'use when' flat.txt
scenarios.judge: D2 of the house standard: a description must never summarize the skill's workflow, because Claude follows the summary instead of reading the body. The draft is a pure workflow summary. Score 5 if the response identifies that summarizing the workflow is the defect (not merely that it is too long or poorly worded) AND rewrites it as trigger conditions. Score 3 if it rewrites well without naming the reason. Score 1 if it accepts the draft or only shortens it.
scenarios.note: The rewrite is the easy half — an unaided agent will shorten a long description. The discriminating half is naming WHY workflow summaries fail, which is a measured finding in this repo's own testing rather than general advice.

scenarios.prompt: I have a spec for a multi-step migration. Write me an implementation plan with phases and validation gates.
scenarios.note: Nearest neighbour is writing-plans. Both author a structured document from requirements, and 'write me a ... plan' is the collision. Hard-gated here rather than left to B10's 0.9 aggregate.

positive: how do I write a new skill for this repo
review this SKILL.md before I ship it
what should this skill's description say
negative: write me an implementation plan for this spec
explain what changed in this commit
record an architecture decision for this
